name: llama.cpp decode on 2x MI50 with -sm tensor: 71.2 tok/s for gpt-oss-120B MXFP4 (and layer split is FASTER at 81.7)
methodology: llama-bench, -p 16384 -n 8192 -b 2048 -ub 1024 -ngl 99 -mmp 0 -dio 1 -fa 1 -o md -r 3 -sm tensor, 2 GPUs via HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 (2x32752 MiB, gfx906:sramecc+:xnack-, wave size 64). Decode figure is tg8192 = 8192 generated tokens, so it is steady-state decode at a long context, not TTFT or a short-context number. Same run with default (layer) split: pp16384 914.81 +/- 0.52, tg8192 81.72 +/- 0.44 - i.e. tensor split is WORSE for decode on this 2-card PCIe node. Not stated by the reporter and therefore NOT recorded: ROCm version, clock/power state, PCIe generation and lane width, host CPU. build hash ff5ef82.
notes: COMMUNITY-REPORTED MEASUREMENT, not a verified benchmark. Pasted in full by the mx-llama.cpp maintainer (mxxm3679) in the gfx906 Discord #llama-cpp channel on 2026-04-22, including the exact command line, device enumeration, and stddev over 3 repeats. Treat as a self-reported practitioner run. Reproducible is null rather than false because essential methodology is missing: without the ROCm version, the SCLK state and the PCIe topology, a re-run is not a like-for-like comparison - and this community's own reporting shows clock and topology move these numbers by tens of percent. The headline finding worth keeping is the layer-vs-tensor comparison, which was run back-to-back on the same machine in the same session and is therefore a fair A/B despite the missing metadata.
